incident_description:
Caller's address is a second address where he lives 6 months out of the year and also works various repair projects for those living around him.

He returned to this address in April 2012 to find that his neighbor/friend had left a push mower on his deck.  The model has handle stubs that push into blade area for storage.

Plastic molding fits at back of deck w/two 18" long handle stubs, the U shaped handle portion bolts to the stubs.

The problem being reported with this option is that the caller's neighbor/friend had purchased one of these mowers, the seller didn't put the screws/stubs in when assembling mower.

The first few times the purchaser used the mower it worked well but when he took it out of the garage maybe the fourth time, the handle began going down into the cutting area because the screws/stubs were not in place.

Caller and his neighbor/friend are satisfied with retailers reaction to problem because the mower was replaced with a different design/model and those remaining in stock were removed.

Caller states that if CPSC will send In Field representative he would be happy to accompany that person to display and discuss the safety issue. 

Caller contacted the manufacturer around June 12th, 2012, doesn't know the name of the person he spoke with. 
He believes that the female in parts department avoided his safety issues and questions.

He is reporting that this is a very dangerous design that needs to be revised.  
When handle approaches a moving blade and chances that a piece could become sliced off then it could fly out and injure the user or those near the mower.

He would request that production of this design be ceased immediately and the mower become recalled.

I have talked to [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and [REDACTED] in addition to the local Home Depot.  These mowers are shipped in boxes with the handle stubs locked in the bottom position with the locking screws.  They all stated that they had problems with people trying to start the units with the handles in the down position.  They had not realized what could happen if the handle were allowed to enter the blade area when the units are running.  [REDACTED] also makes these units under [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] Brand names plus other possible Brand Names.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard with the mower's design, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

I purchased a gas grill from the Tractor Supply Company in [REDACTED], CT  on 5/19/23. It came fully assembled. A few days after I decided to grill, and
hooked up the propane. For some reason the grill would not light, and I could not figure out why. I looked underneath,
and the hose for the regulator was kinked as it was bent at a 90-degree angle. I called the store to see if they had one
from another grill they could swap out. They did not. I spoke with [REDACTED] in customer service who transferred me to [REDACTED]
who put the grill together. He said that "They all come in like that" and there was nothing he could do. So, hes telling
me that every grill they have is defective, and a safety hazard, and the only way for it to work is to take a hose bend it
back creating even more stress on an already defective part that will eventually break. This is a safety hazard that can
result in an explosion. I contacted the [REDACTED] Fire Marshal's office. While they agreed with me they could not help as
they are in charge of grills assembled in a store. If It was in my house in [REDACTED] they could do something about it, but I
live in [REDACTED]. So I'm writing to this department to investigate, and take corrective action not only on this store, but
apparently ever single Tractor Supply Company in Connecticut as if these grills all "come in this way" it is a safety

uploads.

I previously contacted the CT Department of Consumer Protection, but they said to contact you.

incident_description:
My John Deere L-110 Riding lawn tractor was parked in my garage and had not been used in over a week. During the overnite period of May 15, to the morning of May 16, 2011 my three car garage
filled with gasoline vapors to the point that it was unbearable to enter the garage. Had the hot water heater in my garage been a gas type instead of electric my house would have been destroyed by the explosion and ensuing fireball, possibly killing me, my wife and our two children.
 After carefully opening the garage doors manually so as not to create a spark I let the garage air out which took one and a half hours. When it was safe to reenter the garage I traced the gasoline 
vapors to the John Deere. Upon closer examination I could see that the gasoline was leaking out of the lower right side seam of the fuel tank and creating a large puddle under the machine. As well as
filling the garage with a very large volume of vapors.
justification: The incident involved a significant gasoline leak that could have led to a catastrophic explosion, but no actual injury or death occurred.

We are lucky the propane tank did not combust from the line pulling it over as well. My deck is ruined from the grease. So as I screamed my husband came out and picked everything up and made sure I was ok. So he noticed what happened is the telescoping leg had just went up in the leg and it gave. Why in the world do you have telescoping legs on a hot grill that could give like that? This is extremely dangerous. Had my granddaugter been out there like normal that could have been a much different outcome. God was on our side. However I would fix this before someone gets seriously hurt.

incident_description: When trying to turn on the Princeton Vizz 550 RGB to the white bulb, the white light would never illuminate while the red, green, and blue lights would. I must have inadvertently left the headlamp on the white setting and set it down, because when I tried to pick it up roughly 10-15 minutes later, I nearly burned my hand and dropped it. I did not immediately test the compartment at that point, but I popped the batteries out. Instead, I left the batteries removed to recreate the same conditions with the same batteries. When I placed the batteries back in, validated the lamp turned on the red/green/blue lights, I "turned on" the white light again (note - it still did not illuminate). Instead, I monitored the battery compartment with an instant read thermometer and clocked over 190 degrees Farenheit. I tested this again with a completely new, out of box, batteries that did not come bundled with the lamp and got similar results. I've already contacted the company and they are issuing a "tested care package", but I wanted to raise this concern before someone "torched" their forehead with this headlamp.
justification: The incident describes a near-injury (burn risk) and a confirmed overheating hazard, indicating potential for injury if used improperly.

incident_description:
We purchased a Toro Recycler Mower last year from Home Depot. Right away we noticed mulch, rocks and grass flying out at us from a gap in between the mower and the clippings bag. We notified Toro immediately. They were aware of problem saying a "few" customers experienced this problem. Their repair was a small foam piece that stuck on to the catcher opening and closed the gap between the mower and the bag. 

This worked moderately well for a few months, but when the foam compressed, the rocks, mulch and grass came shooting out at us again whenever the mower was in operation. The clippings bag also shoots out grass clippings and dust. It appears as though the weave of the clippings bag is not tight enough, there are numerous holes in the material that allows unacceptable amounts of clippings and dust to be blown out at the user. Its unbearable to use the mower without a mask and eye protection. 

Toro will not refund our purchase price and take back the defective and dangerous mower. 

We feel this mower should be recalled since their only solution is to send out another foam piece which is temporary at best and does not address the defective clippings bag. 

We have seen problems with the Toro recycler mower in the past year that lead to a recall with the blade. We feel this is another issue that warrants a recall on the Toro Recycler Mower.
justification: The mower ejects debris and dust at the user, posing a risk of injury if protective gear is not worn, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
I have investigated two accidents now involving Bad Boy zero turn mowers. One of these accidents involved a consumer and one involved an older gentleman that mowed yards. In both instances the accidents were the result of the mowers running over and onto the victims.
I have inspected both mowers and they do not meet the requirements of the ANSI B71 standards to:
ANSI B71.4-2004 indicates in Section 4.5.8 "Operator-presence controls" and specifically paragraph 4.5.8.1 "Ride-on units and ride-on turf tractors" that:
"A means shall be provided that automatically stops or disengages the traction drive when the operator leaves the normal operator position."
The forseeability of this type of accident is demonstrated by the Appendix to ANSI B71.4 which indicates with respect to paragraph 4.5.8.1 that:
"The requirement for a traction drive Operator Presence Control (OPC) is intended to address run-over type accidents associated with machine movement when the operator leaves the normal operator position. This requirement does not allow the machine traction drive to be operational when the operator is out of the normal operator position."
The design of both machines, unlike many other manufacturers, does not require the travel control levers to be in neutral and the park brake applied before the operator can dismount. This allows a travel lever to be contacted and moved from neutral as the operator dismounts or is getting off the mower such that it moves in a fast turn and can knock the operator down and run up on them.
justification: The description mentions two accidents where the mowers ran over victims, indicating severe outcomes. The design flaw makes such accidents likely if the issue is not addressed.

incident_description:
I am a Certified Fire Investigator with the ATF and recently investigated a fatal fire that was caused by the ignition of potting soil (specifically Miracle Gro potting soil).  The container was plastic, half-filled with dried out potting soil on a covered balconey, sitting adjacent to wood siding and below a window.  Aided by wind, cigarettes that had been discarded in the container ignited the potting soil and the plastic container, which then spread to the siding and into the adjacent apartment.  This fire spread throughout a 12 unit apartment building and resulted in the death of an occupant who was not able to escape in time.  

I have been a fire investigator since 2007 and have encountered multiple fires caused by the ignition of structures after dried out potting soil or peat moss was ignited when cigarettes were discarded within plant containers.  In talking to victims, everyday average people, and even other fire investigators, this fire causation is not widely known.  The publication Fire Findings did a study on this phenomenon in its Spring 2009 issue, Vol. 17, No. 2.  

I believe that lives could be saved and millions of dollars of fire damages could be avoided every year if warning labels were present on bags of potting soil, peat moss, and other similar soil amendments.  The general public is not aware of the fire hazards associated with these products and needs to be educated about the dangers.
justification: The incident resulted in a death and widespread property damage, indicating high severity. The investigator notes multiple similar incidents, suggesting the likelihood is possible.

incident_description:
On May 17, 2022, I purchased a MB20070122 digital smoker and the MB20100112 cold smoker attachment. I ran into two problems last week:
1) Near the end of a six hour smoke, the slow and cold smoker appeared to get very, very hot. I'm not sure why the heating element got so hot, but it was enough to melt the switch and wiring and threw both my GFCI and the breaker in the panel. Plugging in the slow and cold smoker now throws the GFCI. Needless to say, I cannot use it anymore.
2) I went to use the original wood hopper attachment; it appears that the latch for the cold smoker actually tore into the wood chipper housing making it unusable.

I contacted Masterbuilt right after this happened on 11/27. They got back to me after a week with no information. The only question was if I was using an extension cord. In fact, I was, but it is outdoor rated and of sufficient gauge so that it never got hot. My primary use of the extension cord is to keep the smoker away from the house.

In short:
*) What happened that made you want to report? Cold smoker caught on fire and melted on/off switch
*) What type of product(s) were being used? Masterbuilt Slow Smoker https://www.masterbuilt.com/products/masterbuilt-slow-smoker-1 Part #MB20100112 
*) Who was using the product(s)? Me, an adult male living in the United States
*) How were the product(s) being used? A three to six hour smoke for turkey breast
*) Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product? A fire could have caused more damage had the smoker been next to the house. Or had it caught on the grass under the smoker.
*) How did any injuries occur? N/A
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and equipment damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The product in question is the GREENWORKS 40-VOLT 20" DUAL-BLADE Li-ION BATTERY-POWERED LAWNMOWER, MODEL 25302.

I bought this lawnmower, serial number GWT0510399-02/20/14, through Target Stores (on-line mail order, with order number 102506043369) on April 30, 2015.  When the lawnmower developed a serious safety problem (see below), a similar replacement lawnmower (Model 25302) was sent to me by Greenworks' post-sales support representative, Sunrise Global Marketing Inc., in June 2015.  The serial number of the replacement unit is GWT0510445-02/20/14. 

The total area of my lawn (total of front and back) is about 4,800 square feet.  This area is flat, except for a steep slope on one side of the front yard.  

I used the first lawnmower (above) several times, with no problem.  However, on or about May 21, 2015, I noticed that the bail was repeatedly failing to electrically disconnect the electric motor when the bail was released.  (The bail is the safety bar that must be kept depressed in order to maintain an electrical connection to the motor.)  When the bail is released, it is supposed to disconnect the electric motor.  Failure to disconnect is a SERIOUS SAFETY PROBLEM because, in the event that the lawnmower starts to slide back toward the user on a slope, the electric motor must be quickly stopped to prevent extreme injury.  When release of the bail fails to stop the electric motor, the only way to stop the motor is to manually pull out the circuit key, or manually pull out the battery, either of which takes a number of seconds to perform.  

I called the Greenworks support representative, Sunrise Global Marketing (telephone 888-909-6757) and explained the safety problem to them.  They made arrangements for a replacement unit (see above for the S/N) to be sent to me through their office in Mooresville, NC (telephone 704-660-2800).  I received the replacement unit on June 9, 2015.  The Sunrise Global Marketing reference number for this transaction is 1133884.  During June, July, and August, I used the replacement unit several times with no safety problem.  

Then, on September 19, 2015, while I was mowing my lawn, the replacement unit repeatedly displayed the same safety problem as the original unit: RELEASE OF THE BAIL WOULD NOT STOP THE ELECTRIC MOTOR.  

On September 19, 2015, I called Sunrise Global Marketing at telephone 888-909-6757, and also the retailer, Target Stores, and reported the latest safety problem.  I sought to return the lawnmower and obtain a refund.  Both organizations advised me that the lawnmower could not be returned.
justification: The bail failure is a serious safety issue that could lead to injury if the lawnmower slides on a slope, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Submitted to Saferproducts.gov 16 Jul 2013

I originally purchased our mower in Indiana, on 14 Oct 2008 (nearly the end of the mowing season).  At that time our property was less than 1/5th acre. In Dec 2012 we moved to Ocala, Fl. and now have nearly an acre.  We also now have a 52" riding mower for the majority of work, and this mower is very lightly used in some small spaces around bushes and such. 

I have had nothing but problems with this mower since purchase. The latest problem (&last straw for this junk) was a catastrophic fuel leak which occurred 07-15-2013. The fuel tank appears to be designed as a two piece tank with a seam seperating the upper and lower halves.  

I used the mower 2 weeks ago with no incident, cleaned it up and put it away.  So after it sitting for two weeks with an empty tank I pulled it out of the garage. Apparently Toro and B&S still haven't learned their lessons with this tank design.  Search Toro 20071 or 20073 fuel leak and you will see what I mean.  I don't believe Toro is 100% responsible but they continue to use this engine/design.  Apparently this tank is interchangeable to other B&S engines. incident_description:
As I was operating the snow throw through appx 8-10 inches of snow near the edge of the sidewalk, I noticed the chute bouncing around more than normal. As I continued to throw the snow with the machine, the snow discharge chute completely came off of the chute base and landed on the sidewalk as the machine continued to throw snow for a short time until I disabled the auger. 
Upon inspection, I noticed that the plastic chute base (the part that holds the chute to the machine) was completely cracked through/broken on appx 75% of its three shoulders (see photos). The single bolt holding the chute to the base worked its way out of the chute base hole it was designed to be placed in, but remained in the chute itself. I believe this was due to the normal pressure of snow being ejected from the chute. It seems the bolt rose up and out of the hole it was designed to be placed in due to being unsecured with a nut. The repeated pulsating pressure/stress on the plastic chute base shoulders (and no nut to hold the bolt securely in place) was too much for the plastic chute base to handle, it cracked, and subsequent pulsation of snow discharge quickly lifted it up and off of the base.
**The dangerous aspect is that the instruction manual "Assembly Instructions" directs the consumer to "Attach the chute to the snow output port using the bolt and washer (Fig. 3)." There is NO mention of affixing a nut to the bolt in the instructions! Later that night I read through the manual again and came across an exploded parts diagram in the back of the manual that reveals a nut beneath the bolt. 
Any consumer who wishes to be protected by the Warranty Coverage understands that one must do what is asked in the "Assembly Instructions" to have Warranty protection. For this reason, I believe it likely that other consumers also followed the faulty assembly instructions and are likely to encounter the same hazardous situation (chute coming completely off in full operation) after several uses. In my case, appx 10 since purchase.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (chute detachment) but no injury occurred. The likelihood is high as the faulty assembly instructions could lead to similar incidents.

incident_description:
I have a Harman Pellet Stove XXV-TC / year 2018 (S/N  HF 1672177) by Hearth and Home Technologies. Installed June 2019.  The stove started to not follow the set room temperature by 10-15 deg or more on the hot side. Called the Harman technician and was told to load/reload new firmware (firmware update is 21.04.20) .  I did so 5 or 6 times, and each time something changed the stove settings (for good or bad) .   The last firmware download seemed to fix the "following the room temp" issues, but now the stove has safety issues.  
1. When the hopper lip is opened the fans (combustion and room) should stop as they did before.  They do not after firmware update.
2. When the load door is opened the fans (combustion and room) should stop as they did before, it does stop feeding pellets.   If the load door glass would break the combustion fan would not stop running (possible fire hazard).
3. The Touch Screen on/off "button" does not stop the stove. The stove keeps feeding pellets in the off position.  To stop the stove I must open the load door 
 and scrap the hot/burning pellets into the stove's ash pan. Leave the load door cracked open (so it will not feed pellets and start the fire up again) and let it cool for around 45 mins so it will shut down.  If I would unplug the stove it my damage it or smoke up the house.
4. You cannot tell if the firmware has been successful in its download (all downloads ended like they were successful).  You must run the stove to see what is fixed or not fixed. 
5. Was told by the Harman tech it maybe the Touch Screen if the firmware does not work, but the firmware seems to be the problem. Should the Touch Screens not be recalled if it is not the firmware? Or a new/better firmware to update with?
Read on web sites and [REDACTED] pages about the same thing happening to my Harman stove is happening the other stoves.

Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled electric blowers and contact One World Technologies, Inc. for a free replacement." 
[REDACTED]



Please confirm to me though your Safety Department whether I am to receive a replacement leaf blower or a refund; and how this leaf blower product defect is being addressed.

Thank you. 
[REDACTED]

_______________________________

Because this defect has already caused personal injuries in their electric cord model of the exact same design,  and because Im receiving no response, I have called Ryobi numerous times only to be told by their Customer Service people that my complaint is at the Products Safety Department in a stack of complaints and will be tended to on an as received basis which should be in 10 to 14 business days.  They refused to escalate it nor allow me to talk to anyone in their Safety Department.  This is irresponsible and outrageous.  I ask that you folks contact them and request that they recall this product before more people get injured.  

Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that could have caused injury, but the user was not seriously injured.

incident_description:
(06/26/2018) The consumer stated that he disconnected the hose from one grill to a small two- burner camp stove. He heard a noise and found out that gas was flowing out of the end of the hose.
This indicates that the safety valve is defective which makes the product unsafe. 

The consumer stated that there is suppose to be an internal safety valve to prevent the gas from flowing out of the hose.

(06/26/2018) The consumer contacted the firm and was transferred to a supervisor. The consumer provided the information about the incident.
justification: Gas leakage due to a defective safety valve poses a fire or explosion hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In 2003 my nose was broken while transferring my Yardy yard-waste cart to the street for curbside pick-up.  I am uncertain exactly how it happened, but I was rolling it across a relatively flat area of the lawn, perhaps striking a partially exposed tree root or a grass divot.  In any event the Yardy tipped and the edge of the lid struck me squarely across the nose, causing immediate heavy bleeding.  We have subsequently moved and no longer reside at the location of the accident. To my knowledge the unit is still in use at the address where the accident occurred.

My wife took me to the Emergency Room where I was informed I had a 'clean' nose fracture and no setting of the bone would be required; they said it would heal on its own.  I recall the X-ray Tech telling me, "You're not the first one of these that I've seen!"

My nose healed, but I was later informed I now had a deviated septum.  Progressively I found my right nostril closing when I slept on my left side, causing severely restricted airflow thru the right nostril.  It got to the point where I went to an ENT specialist and he performed surgery to correct the deviated septum on 3/29/2011.  It is now early Novemnber of 2011 and I have scheduled another appointment with the specialist, as the right nostril is again causing restricted airflow.  

Prior to the Yardy incident, I never experienced breathing problems through my nose.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken nose and subsequent deviated septum requiring surgery, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) since it was a specific, isolated event with no indication of recurrence.

incident_description: The Solo (brand) hand held sprayer used to mist house plants exploded in my hands when I was pumping it up. The heavy plastic bottle sent plastic "shrapnel" up to 25 feet away. I felt lucky that one of the small pieces did not hit me in the eyes, which could have been catastrophic. These pumps should have a pressure relief valve like garden tank sprayers do to prevent this from happening. I have a picture of the aftermath of the incident.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing plastic shrapnel but no actual injury occurred, though the potential for eye injury was noted.

incident_description: I was mowing uphill and suddenly for no reason lost power to move forward and brakes also failed.  The lawn tractor and I both ended up in the trees/brush line at the bottom of hill.  Thankfully not the creek that is just past the trees. After getting it towed out and into the shop they say the transaxle is broke. My mower is a Cub Cadet SLTX 1054 model # 13WK92AK010, Serial #1F180H60078.  The transaxle #618-04270B and the transaxle serial number is 0161H10033.  It does not appear to be on the recall list, but it is near the same time of manufacture and resulted in the same incident that other models were recalled for.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (lawn tractor) but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Jenn-Air Built-In Gas Grill Model # 750-0142 Lowes SKU # 168935. As I understand it, this grill was manufactured by NexGrill and sold under the Jenn-Air brand name. 

After replacing the steel rod cooking grids on at least three occasions, it has become apparent that there is a serious manufacturing defect in this portion of the product. 

What has me very concerned is how they are manufactured. The grids are advertised as Stainless Steel. I am no expert, however, it appears that they are actually made of steel rods that are then dipped with a stainless steel coating. The end result is that after about 4-6 months of normal usage the outer stainless steel coating begins to separate and razor sharp pieces of steel flake off of the grids. This is bad enough, however, even more dangerous is the fact that those razor sharp pieces stick to the food you are cooking, causing an extremely dangerous hazard should someone ingest or swallow a piece of this steel flake. I have photos to illustrate the issue visually if you would like me to send them to you.
justification: The description indicates a manufacturing defect causing razor-sharp steel flakes to contaminate food, posing a serious ingestion hazard.

incident_description: On July 23, 2011 I purchased a CharBroil RED 4-burner infrared grill.  Within two months of purchase, the labels for the settings of the burner began to peel off.  Now three months later, the labels are nearly totally removed.  This has created a SERIOUS safety issue, whereas it is becoming very difficult to tell if the burners are on or off.  When I contacted CharBroil, they concurred that there was an problem with the grill.  Their answer (case [REDACTED]) was that I could pay to have new parts shipped to me and either I could install them or I could pay someone to install the parts for me.  When I refused to pay money so I could fix the defective grill they closed the warranty claim and considered it resolved.  This is unacceptable for a grill with such a serious safety defect that is only 3 months.
justification: The peeling labels create a safety hazard by making it difficult to determine if the burners are on or off, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Troy-Bilt TB80 EC 2-cycle Trimmer August 26, 2011.

On my first use I found that the design resulted in my right forearm resting on the top of the engine housing.  I tried adjusting the position of the D-handle.  That did not fix the problem.

The engine housing, after just a few minutes use, is hot enough to burn my arm.

I sent an E-mail to Troy-Bilt requesting help.  The Troy-Bilt Question Reference # is [REDACTED].  Troy-Bilt responded 9/9/11 as follows:

"For liability reasons, we are not permitted to assist customers with unapproved modifications that have not been tested and approved by our Safety and Compliance Department. 
If you wish to perform any such alterations or modifications, you will need to do so without our approval. 
Your understanding is appreciated."

The trimmer present a burn hazard.
justification: The trimmer's design causes the engine housing to get hot enough to burn the user's arm, posing a burn hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that a plastic flashlight projecting Halloween images is a potential burn hazard. The product comes with no instructions, no warning and no batteries. The consumer attempted to place a battery into the flashlight and within 5 seconds the battery casing became very hot, within 15 seconds the plastic casing began to blister and melt. The consumer placed it in her sink and watched it blister and smoke. The consumer powered off the toy at the switch using a pot holder and the smoking subsided. The consumer stated that it took 30 minutes to allow the product to cool. 

After the product cooled down the consumer opened the battery compartment and found that her batteries melted and had battery acid over her hand. The consumer called the media and will inspect the product. The consumer called the firm yesterday and left a message. The firm called her back the same day told that they would have the product recalled. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. 

The consumer stated that the product has not caused damage to her home. The consumer was burned to her right hand on her inner palm but not any substantial burns. The consumer has called the fire department after the incident took place. The product takes AA batteries and does not indicate on the packaging to what ages the product is intended.
justification: The consumer suffered burns to her hand, indicating an injury, and the product's design flaw makes similar incidents likely.

incident_description:
Ryobi Leaf Blower model P2108 under normal operation on Sept 1,2018 fan blades broke apart flying out of unit and cut my leg. Minor cut but it was under three year warranty with box and receipt so I called Ryobi and 
reported it and they said someone would call me. After two weeks I calked again and to date I have never received a return phone call.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut) from broken fan blades, and the likelihood of such a failure under normal operation is possible but not common.

incident_description: I was digging up dirt to lay pavers to extend my patio,  I transfered the dirt to the front yard, when I pushed the wheel barrel forward up a slight incline, it rolled back towards me, as it began to turn over to my right,the loop shaped handle pinned me against the wheel barrel. my foot against the wheel and my leg against the loop in the handle. I was knocked to the ground, unable to get free of the wheel barrel. My tibula plataeu was fractured, my madiscus torn, and ligaments in my foot injured. I was on crutches for 4 months, unable to drive or work, after being allowed to walk without crutches, because of my knee, further treatment was nessessary for my ankle and foot. the accident occurred on april 22, 2016 and have only since this February of 2017, been able to walk up or down steps except one at a time
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured tibia plateau, torn meniscus, and foot ligament injuries, requiring prolonged recovery and treatment, indicating a severe injury.

incident_description:
The fuel cap of my Stihl leaf blower BR350 does not reliably seal fuel tank.  This resulted in spilled fuel on me when lifting the blower. In addition to being annoying, this could result in a fire if near an ignition source, including the muffler of the blower. 
I contacted the manufacturer and requested a replacement fuel cap but the manufacturer refused.
justification: Fuel spillage occurred but no injury was reported, though there is a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: I was using my TROY-BILT leaf blower to blow the water off my truck after I washed it and the fan housing exploded. I had the blower at shoulder height as I was blowing the water off the truck hood when it exploded. The internal fan broke apart sending shrapnel everywhere, I was hit in the neck and 3/4 of the fan stayed together and hit me in the shoulder. I had two lacerations on my neck which thankfully did not do serious damage, instead just bled for 10 to 15 min. The big chunk of fan that hit my shoulder created a softball size bruise because it busted one of the veins that runs across my deltoid. It also busted the skin and bled a little through my shirt. I am blessed because I realize this could have been much worse, especially soo close to my head and eyes. I have a handful of pics to go with my claim, my wife was standing 4 feet away when it happened and she thought I some how got electrocuted when she heard the Big Bang and I dropped the blower and jumped away.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations and a significant bruise, indicating injury but no death or serious harm.

incident_description: I have a "Utilitech LED Handheld Flashlight" that I bought at "Lowes" ("Item #: 352081"--"Model #: FTNH2AA1L"). I have had it less than a year.  I was using the same batteries that came with the flashlight (UTILITECH AA). The light did not come on. So, I clicked it several more times. Still, there was no light. Instead of placing it back into my clothing drawer, I placed it on top of my dresser drawers. I woke up about three hours later to change the batteries. The flashlight was extremely hot. I removed the batteries, but I could not hold them in my hand for they were very hot ... hot enough that I had to drop them. They felt as if they was going to burn my hand. I placed the batteries onto my granite counter-top. Two hours later, I replaced the batteries, and turned on the flashlight for about five minutes. The same thing happened again. So, I tried new batteries ([REDACTED]). I received a blister on my hand, and the light did not work. Also, to inform you, we have never dropped this flashlight.
justification: The incident resulted in a blister, indicating an injury, and the recurrence suggests a possible likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The consumer was cutting grass on his riding lawn mower on an incline. His wife was bringing him the cell phone.  He lost the brakes and steering before she got close.  Immediately after losing control, he ran into a tree causing injury to himself and the machine.  At the moment the consumer lost control of the tractor and drove 20 additional feet before crashing into a tree. The consumer stated that there was not rain or inclement weather the day of the incident. The consumer did not fall out of the riding lawn mower as he able to catch his balance.

 The consumers wife helped him off the tractor and allowed him to rest his back on the couch. The consumer felt much worse the next day. The consumer went to his doctor at Pinnacle hospital in Union Deposit, PA on September 16. The consumer given a CAT scan for his back.  The consumer stated that he had no bent rods of any sort to his metal implants. The consumer does have some inflammation to his back and was given ibuprofen. He is now on pain medication prescribed by family physician.

The consumer took the tractor to a local dealer in September and found that the cause was a failure of the steering and braking system. The consumer was doing his independent research and found numerous report of these incidents, citing insufficient hydraulic fluid. The consumer has a previous medical history with his spine concerning his neck vertebrae, back and hip in the last 3 years. 

The consumer has not called the retailer since they are now out of business. The consumer has not had any prior problems with this product. The consumer called the firm about the product in September at 3 different location nationwide including CA, OH and GA and was told that there was nothing that could be done for him because his product was out of warranty. The consumer stated the product is in good apparent condition but the front end has a dent.
justification: The consumer sustained injuries requiring medical attention, including a CAT scan and pain medication, due to the lawn mower's steering and braking failure.

incident_description:
Tractor Supply 25 ton County Line Log Splitter built by YTL
I am writing to complain about the design of the county line log splitter tongue latch.  I broke my hand trying to use this device.  The instructions say to kick the stand latch but because I have a bad hip I can not do that at age 69.  The latch is dangerous.  It snaps with such force it broke my hand.  It appears the manufacturer and retail know of the design flaw.  In fact the CPSC has recieved a similar report 2147393355.  I contacted the 1800 number for serivce and they said they could do nothing.  I called 4 differenct times over the course of 3 months.  I am disappointed in how seriously, or the lack thereof that TSC is taking over this.
justification: The user suffered a broken hand due to the log splitter's design flaw, indicating an injury (severity 3). The mention of a similar CPSC report suggests the issue is possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
A water pump (under warranty) malfunctioned in my farm shed and scalded my arm with first, second and third degree burns, as diagnosed by a medical doctor. A Drummond 63407 Harbor Freight Tools water pump pressure switch failed (and some research shows this happens approx. 11% of the time), but the manufacturer has refused to make an insurance claim to pay me a settlement for my severe injuries (which could have disfigured or killed a child), which restricted my piano teaching income, damaged my property, or pay repair costs. This cheap made pump, the company owned by a Chinese company, is a danger to the American people; especially, children.

UPDATED ON 2/28/2023: [2nd and 3rd degree scalding burns from water and steam from malfunctioning water pump that scalded [REDACTED] June 16, [REDACTED]

UPDATED ON 4/27/2023: [The transfer from the pressure tank to the control switches somehow stuck the pump in an on position. The impeller heated the water in the chamber, and shear friction made very hot water. 

The water pump demonstrated an Initial Break in Failure, or the early part of the Weibull Distribution Failure curve. This process most likely was Value Engineered to a point that it was no longer capable of a high performance or lengthy life cycle time before failure. Consequently, the early failure of a component which needs a redesign. 

The motor drives the impeller, which pumps the water into the pressurized tank. The switch allows the motor to operate (switch on) when the tank pressure falls to 30 PSI and switch off at 50 PSI. The off switch did not engage, and the motor kept spinning the impeller and pumping water to nowhere. The hydrodynamic shear friction in the impeller housing caused the water to heat, and eventually boil. The boiling water formed a two phase system with one side water vapor and the other side boiling water. This spun around with the impeller in a very imbalanced process, and the pump assembly then shook until the boiling water was able to break free and the electric energy discontinued. In this final process, Ms. Hays was burned with first, second and third degree burns, as diagnosed by Brian D. Cooke, MD, Osawatomie, Kansas. 

Eccentric dynamic load released boiling water under pressure. 

The cut off switching apparatus failed, the churning friction in the impeller housing heated and boiled the water and partly
turned the water into steam, a large miss balance in the impeller shook the unit, the pipe broke and boiling water was
sprayed about.]
justification: The incident resulted in first, second, and third degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The failure rate is reported at 11%, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
I purchased a Portfolio outdoor post light #0109348, from Lowes.com. It had 18 side glass panels, and all 18 glass panels were loose. The panels were not properly secured during manufacturing.  All of the nuts on the panel retaining rods were loose, and seven of the nuts had actually fallen off into the packaging. This allowed the glass panels to rattle around and chip or crack. 

As I unpacked the light fixture, prior to installation, I sliced my left thumb open on a one-inch glass shard that was protruding from the bubble wrap.  I could not see the glass shard, and had no reason to expect it prior to examining the light. I have saved the glass shard. 

I believe the glass shard chipped off one of the loose glass panels, causing a danger to anyone who tries to unpack or install one of these lights. 

I have contacted Lowes several times, but have received little or no cooperation.  It appears that the Portfolio lights are made by Lowes or a related company.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut injury from a glass shard, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) given the manufacturing defect and loose components.

incident_description: Brand new Endless Summer "Bryson" LP Gas Outdoor Firepit (Model #GAD17104ES caught fire the first time I attempted to use it (after successfully turning it on as a test earlier in the day). I properly connected a new [REDACTED] propane tank. Fire consumed the unit, caused 2nd degree superficial skin wounds to me when the fire flared as I tried to turn off the gas valve (face, arms and hands), destroyed an outdoor rug and several outdoor furniture cushions before the fire department put it out.
justification: The incident caused 2nd degree superficial skin wounds and property damage, indicating an injury severity. The likelihood is possible given the description of the event.

incident_description:
I was using the Craftsman blower and it started on fire.  The motor burned up on it.
I contacted Sears to report the incident, but they said I would have to contact Craftsman which I did.  They did nothing about it.
I saw the recall offer, but when I called about it, they said I wasn't eligible as I no longer had the blower.  I do have documentation that I had purchased the blower from Sears and the box it was in.
I was concerned about the blower and the fire.  I reported it and it should have been easier to get the concern resolved.
justification: The blower caught fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: plugged in Intertek Floodlight model FU 2202 (3rd use since purchase) to light up work area in shed. it was clamped to an adjacent shelf near work table. after about 20 min. of being on fire shot out of bulb socket. unplugged the light immediately and removed it to an outside area. after cooling down I  opened up light  The socket on one end of halogen bulb had been ejected from the socket and burned significantly  the socket itself was burnt and cracked in half.
justification: The floodlight malfunctioned, causing a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
10/31/2022) The consumer stated that the product caught on fire. The consumer had plugged in the product before he left the property. When he came back later, he smelled something. He looked through the window of his house and saw sparks coming from the bug zapper. He went inside, held my breath and unplugged the product. There was a plastic clear smoke smell throughout the house. The clear smoke followed me outside to garage put on respreator too go check for fire in house
Then is when I inhailed clear plastic toxic smoke.

The consumer stated that he inhaled the plastic smoke and had to receive medical attention from the doctor. He had x-rays done. CT scan showed smoke in my lungs after 3 months
justification: The consumer inhaled toxic smoke and required medical attention, including x-rays and a CT scan, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Purchased a barbecue grill from Lowe's on 12/24/2014. 
On February 15, 2016 my wife opened the lid on the barbecue grill which shifted the weight to the rear.  As soon as this happened the back wheels collapsed inward towards the front of the barbecue grill.  The barbecue rolled backwards and off of our patio onto the stone deck below.  My wife was injured trying to grab the handle and save the grill from going over.  Worse- the propane tank was inside and likely could have been ruptured.  The grill was mangled completely.  My wife has pain in her shoulder which we are trying to see a doctor for this week.  Had a person been in the path of this extremely heavy barbecue grill there could have been a life threatening incident.  Had the grill been lit at that point there could have been a fire.  This is extremely worrisome.  
The grill was purchased from Lowe's and was delivered completely assembled by the store.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the wife and potential for severe consequences like fire or propane rupture, indicating a high severity. The likelihood is possible given the described mechanism of failure.
